specification.problem: Estimate a time-varying optical phase \phi(t), modelled as a stochastic phase-noise process with imprecisely known parameters, imprinted on a squeezed state of light and read out by continuous homodyne detection over a fixed interval [0,T]; the estimate is formed by a fixed-interval smoother (using all data on [0,T]) that is made robust to the parameter uncertainty, and its mean-square error is compared with that of the nominal (non-robust) smoother.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction (chosen here as an assumption, since no experiment_scope was supplied): a single-mode, linearized (small-phase) continuous-variable model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck phase-noise process whose damping rate \lambda is uncertain within a known interval, a squeezed-state homodyne measurement model with reduced measurement-noise intensity, a nominal Kalman filter plus Rauch-Tung-Striebel fixed-interval smoother, and a worst-case (min-max) robust smoothing criterion over the uncertainty set. Tiny explicit instance: \lambda_0=1, \delta_\lambda=0.5, \kappa=1, |\alpha|=1, r=0.5, T=2, discretised with \Delta t=0.5 (N=4 samples). Outside scope: the paper's specific robust-smoother synthesis (e.g. guaranteed-cost/H_\infty Riccati equations), the exact phase-noise model and parameter values used in the paper, any adaptive (feedback) homodyne scheme, non-ideal squeezing/loss modelling, and the paper's numerical results. This is a continuous-variable metrology/estimation scheme, not a qubit gate-model algorithm; the quantum part is state preparation and homodyne readout, while filtering/smoothing is classical postprocessing.

equations.label: Phase-noise model (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck)
equations.description: Linear Gaussian stochastic model for the optical phase; \lambda and \kappa are the 'parameters underlying the phase noise'.
equations.justification: A standard phase-noise model in continuous-time optical phase tracking; the abstract only says 'phase noise' with underlying parameters and does not specify the model.
assumptions: Phase noise is a stationary OU process; the paper may use another model (e.g. Wiener process or higher-order noise).

equations.label: Linearized homodyne measurement of a squeezed probe
equations.description: Homodyne photocurrent in the small-phase (linearized) regime; squeezing of the measured quadrature reduces the shot-noise intensity from 1 (coherent state) to approximately e^{-2r}.
equations.justification: Standard linearized continuous homodyne model for phase estimation with squeezed light; the exact noise expression in the paper (including losses, anti-squeezing leakage, or adaptive local-oscillator feedback) is unknown.
assumptions: Ideal pure squeezing with no loss; no adaptive feedback of the local-oscillator phase.

equations.label: Parametric uncertainty in the phase-noise model
equations.description: The true damping rate lies in a known interval around the nominal value; the robust smoother is designed over this set rather than for \lambda_0 alone.
equations.abstract_quote: uncertainties explicitly introduced in parameters underlying the phase noise
equations.justification: The abstract states that uncertainties are introduced into phase-noise parameters; a norm-bounded interval on \lambda is the simplest concrete realization. Which parameters are uncertain, and the uncertainty structure, are not stated.
assumptions: Only \lambda is uncertain and the uncertainty is a deterministic norm-bounded perturbation; \kappa could also be uncertain in the paper.

equations.label: Nominal forward Kalman filter
equations.description: Kalman-Bucy filter for eq_1-eq_2 with the nominal parameter \lambda_0; it is the forward pass of the fixed-interval smoother.
equations.justification: Standard Kalman-Bucy equations for a scalar linear Gaussian system; optimal only when the model is exact, which motivates the robust design in the abstract.

equations.label: Nominal fixed-interval (RTS) smoother, backward pass
equations.description: Rauch-Tung-Striebel backward recursion giving the estimate conditioned on the entire record y(s), 0\le s\le T.
equations.justification: Standard continuous-time RTS fixed-interval smoother; the abstract names a 'fixed-interval smoother' but does not specify which smoother form (RTS, two-filter/Mayne-Fraser) the paper uses.
assumptions: RTS form chosen; the paper may use a two-filter form.

equations.label: Robust smoothing criterion over the uncertainty set
equations.description: Worst-case (guaranteed-cost/min-max) formulation: the robust smoother minimizes an upper bound on the error variance that holds for all admissible parameter perturbations.
equations.abstract_quote: a robust fixed-interval smoother designed with uncertainties explicitly introduced in parameters underlying the phase noise
equations.justification: 'Robust ... designed with uncertainties explicitly introduced' implies a design criterion over the uncertainty set; a worst-case criterion is the generic meaning. The paper's actual synthesis (e.g. modified Riccati equations with uncertainty-dependent terms) is not available from the abstract and is NOT reconstructed here.
assumptions: Min-max mean-square criterion; the specific robust-smoother equations are a missing paper contribution.

equations.label: Performance metric for comparison
equations.description: Time-averaged mean-square estimation error; the claimed improvement is that the robust smoother has lower error than the nominal smoother when the true parameters deviate from nominal.
equations.abstract_quote: exhibits improvement when using a robust fixed-interval smoother
equations.justification: The abstract claims improvement; mean-square error is the standard figure of merit for phase estimation. The magnitude and conditions of improvement are not given.
assumptions: Improvement measured in mean-square error; the inequality is the paper's claim, not verified here.

registers.name: optical probe mode
registers.role: Carries the squeezed state whose phase quadrature is shifted by \phi(t) and read out by homodyne detection

registers.name: classical measurement record
registers.size: N = T/\Delta t real samples (N=4 in the tiny instance)
registers.role: Stores homodyne increments \Delta y_k used by the forward filter and backward smoother

specification.initial_state: Probe mode in a phase-squeezed coherent state |\alpha, r\rangle = D(\alpha)S(r)|0\rangle with \alpha real and squeezing of the phase quadrature; estimator initialised at \hat\phi_f(0)=0 with stationary prior variance P_f(0)=\kappa/(2\lambda_0).

steps.description: Specify the nominal phase-noise model and the uncertainty set for its parameters (tiny instance: \lambda_0=1, \delta_\lambda=0.5, \kappa=1).
Prepare the squeezed probe state and let the true phase process \phi(t) (with some \lambda in the uncertainty set) act on it.
Perform continuous homodyne detection of the phase quadrature over [0,T], recording y(t) (tiny instance: |\alpha|=1, r=0.5, R_{sq}=e^{-1}, T=2, \Delta t=0.5).
Run the nominal forward Kalman filter on the record to obtain \hat\phi_f(t), P_f(t).
Run the backward fixed-interval smoother to obtain the nominal smoothed estimate \hat\phi_s(t).
Design and run the robust fixed-interval smoother over the uncertainty set to obtain \hat\phi_s^{rob}(t) (specific synthesis equations missing from the abstract).
Compare mean-square errors of nominal and robust smoothers for true \lambda\neq\lambda_0.

specification.measurement: Continuous (time-resolved) homodyne detection of the phase quadrature of the squeezed probe, yielding the photocurrent increments dy(t) of eq_2; in the discretised tiny instance, N=4 Gaussian samples \Delta y_k with mean 2|\alpha|\phi_k\Delta t and variance R_{sq}\Delta t.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Forward Kalman filtering (eq_4) followed by backward fixed-interval smoothing (eq_5) for the nominal estimator; a robust fixed-interval smoother (eq_6) designed over the parameter uncertainty set for the robust estimator; evaluation and comparison of the time-averaged mean-square error (eq_7), e.g. by Monte Carlo over sample paths of \phi(t).
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the single-mode OU-noise, linearized-homodyne construction and the tiny instance (\lambda_0=1, \delta_\lambda=0.5, \kappa=1, |\alpha|=1, r=0.5, T=2, \Delta t=0.5, N=4) are the reconstructor's choices, not paper content.
The phase-noise model is Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and only its damping rate is uncertain.
Small-phase linearization of the homodyne signal holds and squeezing is ideal and lossless.
The robust smoother is characterised only by a generic worst-case criterion; the paper's actual robust-smoother equations are not reconstructed.

The scheme is continuous-variable metrology with classical estimation; it is not a qubit gate-model algorithm, so any circuit-generation stage would need a bosonic-mode or Gaussian-state simulator rather than a qubit circuit.
